## Overview

This project investigates immune remodelling in cervical carcinoma using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis.

The workflow includes preprocessing of single-cell transcriptomic data, quality control, normalization, clustering, cell type annotation, differential expression analysis, and immune microenvironment characterization.

## Objectives

- Identify major cell populations in cervical carcinoma samples.
- Characterize immune cell infiltration patterns.
- Explore transcriptional changes associated with tumour progression.
- Identify potential immune-related molecular signatures.

## Methods

The analysis pipeline includes:

- Single-cell RNA sequencing data processing
- Quality control and filtering
- Dimensionality reduction using PCA and UMAP
- Cell clustering
- Marker gene identification
- Cell type annotation
- Differential expression analysis

## Tools and Technologies

- R
- Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis
- Bioinformatics workflows
- Data visualization

## Results

The analysis provides insights into cellular heterogeneity and immune landscape changes within cervical carcinoma tissues.

## Publication / Research Context

This project contributes to understanding tumour immune interactions through computational analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data.
